Fiscal Year 2027 Budget Process

The city's budget planning process has been finalized for fiscal year 2027. Fiscal year 2027 begins on July 1, 2026, and ends June 30, 2027. City Council members can only adopt one fiscal year at a time, even though the city plans for multi-year budgets.

Recorded budget presentations are available online via CTN's YouTube channel. All presentations and materials are posted on this webpage. 

Budget timeline:  

March 23, 2026:  City Council Work Session FY27 Budget Planning

April: In accordance with City Charter, the city administrator's recommended fiscal year 2027 budget is submitted to City Council in April. 

May: City Council, with at least seven affirmative votes, will vote to adopt the budget at its meeting on May 18.

Budget-related feedback or comments are encouraged and may be submitted via email to budget@a2gov.org.

Other budget documents:
FY27 Budget Responses - May 1, 2026
FY27 Budget Responses - May 13, 2026

Fiscal Year 2026/2027 Budget Process

The city's two-year budget planning process has been finalized for fiscal years 2026 and 2027. Fiscal year 2026 begins on July 1, 2025, and ends June 30, 2026. City Council members can only adopt one fiscal year at a time, even though the city plans for multi-year budgets.

Recorded budget presentations are available online via CTN's YouTube channel. All presentations and materials are posted on this webpage. 

Budget timeline:  

March 24, 2025:  City Council Work Session FY25 Budget Planning

April: In accordance with City Charter, the city administrator's recommended fiscal year 2026 budget is submitted to City Council in April. City Council members can only adopt one fiscal year at a time even though the city plans for multi-year budgets.  The Proposed Budget for FY 2026 can be viewed here​.

May: City Council, with at least seven affirmative votes, will vote to adopt the budget at its meeting on May 19.

Budget-related feedback or comments are encouraged and may be submitted via email to budget@a2gov.org.

Fiscal Year​ 2022/23 Budge​​t Process

 

​Budget planning discussions for fiscal years 2022 and 2023 will begin with City Council work sessions in 2021. Fiscal year 2022 begins on July 1, 2021, and ends June 30, 2022. City Council members can only adopt one fiscal year at a time even though the city plans for multi-year budgets.

On Sept. 21, 2020, City Council passed resolution R-20-374 to Conduct a 2020 Budget Priorities Citizen Survey to Inform Development of the City’s FY22 Budget and FY23 Financial Plan via The National Research Center.   

  • Ann Arbor Budget Priorities Survey Report - Jan. 2020​

​City Council work sessions:
The below Council Work Session discussions are scheduled with noted service units to discuss draft budgets. These meetings will be held virtually at 7 p.m. Meetings are streamed live and are available to view later via CTN's YouTube channel https://www.youtube.com/user/ctnannarbor. All presentations and materials will be available on this webpage. 

Feb. 8: City Administrator Area, Finance, Police, Fire, Courts and Community Services.  Presentation and materials.

Feb. 22: Pension, Ann Arbor Housing Commission. Presentation and materials.

March 8:  Public Services and City Attorney's Office. Presentation and materials.

March 22: Downtown Development Authority and SmartZone. Presentation and materials.

Budget timeline: 

January–March: Council work sessions tentatively planned.  

April: In accordance with City Charter, the City Administrator's recommended fiscal year 2022 budget is submitted to City Council on April 19, 2021. City Council members can only adopt one fiscal year at a time even though the city plans for multi-year budgets.

May: City Council, with at least seven affirmative votes, must adopt the budget no later than its second meeting in May (May 17).

Budget-related feedback or comments are encouraged and may be submitted via email to budget@a2gov.org.

Fiscal Year 2020/21 Budget Process

Budget planning discussions for fiscal years 2020 and 2021 begin with City Council Work Sessions in 2019. Fiscal year 2020 begins on July 1, 2019 and ends June 30, 2020. City Council members can only adopt one fiscal year at a time even though the city plans for multi-year budgets.

On Sept. 4, 2018 City Council passed Resolution R-18-360​​ to engage the professional services of The Center for Priority Based Budgeting (CPBB) to conduct a Priority Based Budgeting Survey for the City of Ann Arbor to assist in developing the city budget and spending priorities.   

  • Ann Arbor Budget Priorities Survey Report - Dec. 2018
  • Ann Arbor Budget Priorities Survey Cross-tabulations 

On Dec. 17, 2018, City Council passed R-18-498, which directed the city to design and conduct a scientifically-based and statistically valid follow-up survey of Ann Arbor residents only that is specifically focused on citizen preferences for utilization of the Washtenaw County Mental Health and Public Safety Millage proceeds. 

  • Ann Arbor Millage Survey Report - March 2019​ (PDF)

On April 1, 2019, City Council passed R-19-0565, which directed the City Administrator to Provide Additional Funding in the FY20/21 Budget and Financial Plan to Address Affordable Housing, Climate Action, and Pedestrian Safety and Provide SMART Performance Outcomes.   

​

City Council Work Sessions:
Feb. 11: General Funds (Administration, Community Services, Finance, Fire and Police Services) Presentation and Materials.
Feb. 25: Public Services. Presentation and materials.
March 11: Cost of Services/Water Rates. Presentation and materials.   
April 8:  Transportation. Presentation and materials.
April 22:  Ann Arbor Housing Commission and Downtown Development Authority. Presentation and materials.

Council Work Session discussions with staff for budget purposes will be held at Larcom City Hall, Council Chambers 2nd Floor, 301 E. Huron St. 7 p.m. Meetings will be available to view live in a variety of formats including: Comcast cable channel 16, AT&T UVerse Channel 99 or live webstream. Citizens can also view the meeting later at their convenience via CTN's Youtube channel​. 

Budget Timeline: 
Feb. - March: Council Work Sessions.   
April: In accordance with City Charter, the City Administrator's Recommended fiscal year 2020 budget is submitted to City Council on April 15, 2019. City Council members can only adopt one fiscal year at a time even though the city plans for multi-year budgets.
May: City Council, with at least seven affirmative votes, must adopt the budget no later than its second meeting in May (May 20).

Budget-related feedback or comments are encouraged via e-mail to budget@a2gov.org​.

Budget Timeline: 
February - March: Council Work Sessions held on February 11, 25 and March 11 and 25.  
April: In accordance with City Charter, the City Administrator's Recommended FY2014 and 2015 Budget is submitted to City Council on April 15, 2013. City Council members can only adopt one fiscal year at a time even though the city plans for multi-year budgets.
May: City Council, with at least seven affirmative votes, must adopt the budget no later than its second meeting in May (May 20).

Budget-related feedback or comments are encouraged via e-mail to budget@a2gov.org.

Fiscal Year 2013 Budget

Fiscal year 2013 begins on July 1, 2012 and ends June 30, 2013. This is the second year of the two-year budget presented to Council in May of 2011 by the City Administrator. City Council members can only adopt one fiscal year at a time even though the city plans for multi-year budgets.

Budget Timeline: 
February - March: Council Work Sessions were scheduled for February 13 and March 12.  
April: In accordance with City Charter, the City Administrator's Recommended FY2013 Budget is submitted to City Council on or before April 15, 2012.
May: City Council, with at least seven affirmative votes, must adopt the budget no later than its second meeting in May.

Fiscal Year 2012 Budget

On Saturday, December 4, 2010, City Council held a work session to begin fiscal year 2012 and 2013 budget discussions and prepare staff priorities. This budget discussion regarding sustainable city services will continue at a Council offsite meeting on Saturday, Jan. 8, 2011. In addition, several Council Work Session have been scheduled to continue public budget discussions. Fiscal year 2012 begins on July 1, 2011 and ends June 30, 2012.
